Where it began

Kemar Roach was born in Saint Lucy, Barbados, on 30 June 1988, and played his domestic cricket for Barbados. At 5ft 8in he was short for a fast bowler, but that never slowed him down. As a young man he was regularly clocked at more than 90mph.

He was called into the West Indies Test squad in June 2008 with only four first-class games behind him. He did not play that Test, but later that month he made his international debut in a T20 match against Australia and returned the best figures of the game, 2 for 29.

The player

His Test debut came against Bangladesh in July 2009, and his first wicket was the all-rounder Shakib Al Hasan. In the second Test he took 6 for 48, which would stand as his best Test figures, and he finished as his side's leading wicket-taker in the series. Later that year in Australia he was often bowling at over 150 km/h, and Ricky Ponting was among those who said how good he was. In Sri Lanka in 2010 he was Man of the Series.

At the 2011 World Cup he took a hat-trick against the Netherlands, the first by a West Indian at a World Cup, on his way to 6 for 27. In 2012 he took ten wickets in a Test against Australia, something no West Indian had managed since Corey Collymore in 2005. By November 2026 he had played 91 Tests and taken 304 wickets at 26.95, with 12 five-wicket hauls. That placed him 42nd among all Test wicket-takers.

What made him special

Early on he was all pace, skidding the ball at batters with yorkers, swinging deliveries and the odd short ball. As the years passed he swapped some of that speed for extra movement, and became a craftsman. His 5 for 17 against England at Kensington Oval in 2019 won an award as the Test bowling performance of the year.

With the bat he was a willing helper rather than a run machine. He averaged 12.09 in Tests, though he did once reach 58 not out, a day to treasure. No-balls were an occasional nuisance too. In one Test at Lord's in 2012 he bowled 18 of them, and twice had Alastair Cook caught off one.

Away from the middle

He won the BBL02 title with the Brisbane Heat, taking 3 for 18 in the final against the Perth Scorchers. At Worcestershire in 2011 he learned the English game from the seamer Alan Richardson, and in 2022 he took 25 wickets at 24.04 for Surrey as they won the County Championship.

And finally

His landmarks have a knack for timing. His 100th Test wicket came at Kensington Oval on his twenty-sixth birthday in 2014. His 200th came at Old Trafford in 2020, when he bowled Chris Woakes and became only the ninth West Indian to that mark. The 300th arrived in 2026 against Sri Lanka, in a match the West Indies won by an innings and 217 runs. Some presents are worth the wait.
